{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693787428,"sessionID":"ses_e23ebae55ffeBkMu6UUSYjIHcQ","part":{"id":"prt_1dc15ef0a001wGPGAnK5wev3Lk","messageID":"msg_1dc15d17a001jC39Mar9uA6ykO","sessionID":"ses_e23ebae55ffeBkMu6UUSYjIHcQ","type":"text","text":"I found and fixed four separate faults. From minute 77 to the end of the shift at minute 120, all four customer-facing services were at 0% errors.\n\n| Cause | Customer impact | Fix | Back to normal |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| checkout-svc deploy v85 removed the `orders.write` permission, so requests failed with PermissionDenied. Retries then overloaded checkout-svc. | partner-api ~95% errors (via recommendations-svc and cart-svc) | Rolled back the deploy, then scaled checkout-svc from 4 to 8 replicas to absorb the retries | ~min 30 |\n| sessions-cache deploy v175 fixed its database connection pool at 4, so calls timed out | web-storefront and admin-portal 4% errors (via ranking-svc) | Rolled back the deploy | min 38 |\n| cart-svc deploy v74 (added tracing) ran out of memory and kept restarting, then got stuck in its own retry overload | Part of the partner-api errors | Rolled back the deploy, scaled to 8 replicas for a few minutes, then back to 4 | min 52 |\n| New fault at min 64: banners-svc config change cfg-44 removed `currency` from the price fields | partner-api ~51% errors | Reverted the config | min 77 |\n\n**What cost the most:** rolling back sessions-cache fails 30% of requests while it runs, and callers retry those failures. That overloaded sessions-cache and pushed web-storefront to about 55% errors from roughly minute 24 to 33. Web-storefront earns $15,700/min, so this was the most expensive stretch of the shift. Scaling sessions-cache to 9 replicas cleared it. Scaling it before starting the rollback would have avoided most of this.\n\n**Extra replicas left on until the end:** sessions-cache at 4 (normal is 3) and checkout-svc at 5 (normal is 4). I kept them as headroom because both normally run near capacity, which is what let the retries overload them. They cost $6/min in total.\n\nThere were no throttles, and every mitigation went to a service that actually had a fault.","time":{"start":1794693787402,"end":1794693787425}}}
